Today the clause has ZERO surface: `fileControlClauses` (src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolIO.g4:46) has no collating alternative and `COLLATING` is a hard reserved lexer token (CobolLexer.g4:370), so any file-control COLLATING SEQUENCE is a generic parse error at every --std (probe: COBOL0312 'unexpected COLLATING'). Add one alternative to `fileControlClauses`:
• Format 1 — reuse the EXISTING shared subrule: `COLLATING? SEQUENCE (collatingForPhrase+ | IS? cobolWord cobolWord?)`. `collatingForPhrase` already lives at CobolIO.g4:558 and is shared by SORT/MERGE and PROGRAM COLLATING (CobolParserCore.g4:390); it already encodes the FOR ALPHANUMERIC/FOR NATIONAL choice-indicator 'one-or-more, any order' semantics (§12.4.5.7.2 figure note). The `IS? cobolWord cobolWord?` leg is the `IS alphabet-name-1 [alphabet-name-2]` form.
• Format 2 — a NEW key-level rule: `COLLATING? SEQUENCE OF cobolWord+ IS? cobolWord` (the data-name/record-key-name list, then alphabet-name-3). `OF` is the required disambiguator vs Format 1.

derivations.bindSemantics:
Bind resolves each key's alphabet at compile time and validates SR1–SR8, cloning the proven program-collating validator DataBinder.Switches.cs:266-313 (ResolveProgramCollating) and the SortBinder clone:
• SR1 (§12.4.5.7.3.1): alphabet-name-1 must resolve in the Alphabets registry to an ALPHANUMERIC collating sequence; SR2: alphabet-name-2 must be NATIONAL. SR7 (Format 2): alphabet-name-3's class must match the key's class (national key ⇒ national alphabet, else alphanumeric).
• SR3: at most one file-level Format 1 clause per file control entry. SR8: a given key named in at most one Format 2 clause. SR4/SR5: each Format-2 name must be a declared RECORD KEY or ALTERNATE RECORD KEY of this file. SR6: those names not subscripted.
• FileModel (src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Model/FileModel.cs, no collating member today) gains a per-key alphabet resolution: for each key (prime + each alternate) resolve, in order, (1) a Format-2 alphabet naming it [§12.4.5.7.4 GR6]; else (2) the Format-1 FOR-class default for that key's class [GR2/GR3]; else (3) native [GR4/GR5 = §12.4.5.3 GR6]. The result is a CollatingTable per key (src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/CollatingModel.cs — CollatingTable(ushort[] Positions,…) already exists).
• GR1 'fixed file attribute set at the OPEN that creates the physical file': the resolved per-key sequence is stamped into the emitted registration; the external-file-connector 'same COLLATING SEQUENCE clauses' rule (§13.4.5 g) is a bind-time consistency check for EXTERNAL files. True cross-run persistence of the creation-time alphabet is a runtime/metadata concern (see runtime depth).
derivations.runtimeSemantics:
The entire runtime behavior is per-key ordering + equality by an alphabet-derived weight table, and it concentrates on ONE engine, src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/IO/IndexedConnector.cs:
• §12.4.5.5.3 GR2c — READ NEXT/PREVIOUS yields records 'ascending within a given key of reference according to the collating sequence for that key.' The sole ordering derivation is `Ordered(int keyIndex)` (line 444-445), currently `StringComparer.Ordinal`. This must order by the per-key weights.
• §14.9.41 GR17e — START comparison is 'according to the collating sequence of the file.' `Start` (line 395) and the forward/reverse search must compare partial keys by weights, not `string.CompareOrdinal`; `ReadSequential.PositionCompare` (line 233) and `StartFirstLast` inherit the same table.
• §14.9.27 GR14 — OPEN INPUT/I-O sets the FPI to the LOWEST position 'in the collating sequence associated with the file'; the first READ NEXT therefore depends on the weighted order, satisfied automatically once `Ordered` is weighted.
• §12.4.5.12.4 GR1 / §14.9.35 GR24 tail / §14.9.51 GR35 — key EQUALITY/uniqueness/suppression is 'based on the collating sequence … according to the rules for a relation condition.' Under an alphabet that EQUATES two characters, binary-different keys are EQUAL. So prime-key uniqueness (Write line 294), alternate-key uniqueness (Write line 300 / Rewrite line 337), ReadRandom match (line 254), Rewrite/Delete target lookup (lines 330/336/363), the '02' look-ahead (line 218), and SUPPRESS-WHEN equality must all route through weighted compare, not ordinal `==`.
• §9.1.13 status 21 / §14.9.51 GR38 — the sequential-access ascending WRITE check (`_lastWrittenPrime`, Write line 292) must use the file's prime-key weights, so keys ascending in native order but descending under the alphabet correctly raise '21'.
All sites route through the pre-existing `CobolString.Compare(string?, string?, ushort[] weights)` (src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Values/Text/CobolString.cs:124), equality = `Compare(...)==0`. Weight tables are threaded per key via the IndexedConnector ctor (prime) + an `AddAlternateKey` overload, emitted at KeyedIoEmitter.EmitRegistration (line 41) into FileRegisterIndexed/FileAddAlternateKey, with the ushort[] literal produced by SortEmitter's WeightsExpr pattern (CodeGen/Verbs/SortEmitter.cs:248-261).

testAssertions: DISCRIMINATOR — Format 1 reversing alphabet: `ALPHABET REV` placing 'Z'..'A' (or a literal alphabet inverting two letters); INDEXED prime key; WRITE keys 'A' then 'Z'; sequential READ NEXT loop must return Z then A. Native-ordinal engine returns A,Z — this single case proves the weighted `Ordered`.

START KEY >= operand under the custom alphabet positions to a record that native ordinal ordering would place elsewhere; assert the record made available and the subsequent READ NEXT order (§14.9.41 GR17e).

Equivalence-class alphabet (two characters share a weight): WRITE two records whose prime keys differ ONLY in those characters ⇒ the second WRITE returns duplicate-key '22' (§12.4.5.12 GR1). Ordinal engine accepts both — proves weighted EQUALITY, not just ordering.

Format 2 per-key isolation: prime key native, ALTERNATE key under a custom alphabet; the alternate READ NEXT walk follows the alphabet while the prime walk stays native — proves per-key (Format 2) resolution, not per-file.
FOR ALPHANUMERIC vs FOR NATIONAL split (post-85): an alphanumeric key ordered natively and a national key ordered by alphabet-name-2 in the same file (GR2/GR3).
No-clause regression: a file with no COLLATING SEQUENCE clause keeps native ordinal ordering unchanged (§12.4.5.3 GR6) — the existing NIST-IX goldens must stay green.
Sequential-access ascending WRITE under the alphabet: keys ascending in NATIVE order but descending under the declared alphabet ⇒ status '21' (§14.9.51 GR38 tied to the file collating sequence).

remaining-waves-scout.md:389 characterizes SUPPRESS-WHEN suppression as 'ordinal equality over the file collating sequence (§12.4.5.6.4 GR6 … rules for a relation condition)'. This conflates ordinal with the file collating sequence: GR6/§14.9.51 GR35 tie suppression equality to the file's collating sequence, which is ordinal ONLY when native. Under an equivalence-class alphabet the suppression predicate is NOT ordinal. A precision inversion, mitigated by the scout naming the seam elsewhere.

Today `pictureClause : PIC PIC_STRING ;` (CobolData.g4:340) — a trailing `EDITING ...` does not parse (`--std 2023` probe: `error COBOL0307: unexpected 'FOR'`). No PICMODE restructure is needed: PIC_STRING stops at whitespace and pops mode, so `EDITING` and its literals are already lexed in default mode. New rule per the Format-1 diagram (19951-19967): `editingPhrase : EDITING literal ( IS literal | FOR ( NEGATIVE IS literal (POSITIVE IS literal)? | POSITIVE IS literal (NEGATIVE IS literal)? ) )? ;` — the FOR group's inner braces carry CHOICE INDICATORS (verified in the figure note at 19957/19970), so one FOR phrase may carry NEGATIVE alone, POSITIVE alone, or BOTH in either order (fork3(a) = YES). derivations.construct: VALUE clause Format 2 (table format) + the glued-multi-literal reject (ledger VF4). This IS a DATA DIVISION table-initialization feature, governed by §13.18.63 "VALUE clause", general format "Format 2 (table)" at §13.18.63.2. It initializes SELECTED elements/ranges of an OCCURS table by keying a list of literals to occurrence subscripts via a MANDATORY FROM (subscript) phrase and an optional TO (subscript) phrase. Distinct from Format 1 (data-item, exactly one literal), Format 3 (level-88 condition-name), Format 4 (report-section bare literal list), and Format 5 (content-validation).
